title: Everyday communication
canDo: I can say I'm running late and give a new time
I can introduce myself at work
I can ask politely for help in an office
I can book an appointment by phone
I can write a short email to confirm a meeting

weeklyTask.prompt: Send a voice note saying you'll be late, with a new time.

lessons.title: Calling to say you're running late

dialogue.text: Hello?
dialogue.fr: Allô ?

dialogue.text: Hi Grace. I'm sorry, I'm running late. There's a lot of traffic on Mombasa Road.
dialogue.fr: Salut Grace. Désolée, je suis en retard. Il y a beaucoup de circulation sur Mombasa Road.

dialogue.text: No problem. When will you get here?
dialogue.fr: Pas de souci. Tu arrives quand ?

dialogue.text: I'll be there by 10:30. I'll call you as soon as I arrive.
dialogue.fr: Je serai là vers 10 h 30. Je t'appelle dès que j'arrive.

dialogue.text: Great. See you soon.
dialogue.fr: Super. À tout à l'heure.

words.meaning: going to arrive later than planned
words.example: Sorry, I'm running late.

words.meaning: many cars on the road
words.example: There's a lot of traffic this morning.

words.meaning: arrive at this place
words.example: When will you get here?

words.meaning: at 10:30 or before
words.example: I'll be there by 10:30.

words.meaning: immediately when
words.example: I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

pattern.name: will for promises

explain.en: When you decide or promise something while you are speaking, use will. In speech it is usually short: I'll. After 'as soon as' and 'when', use the present, even for the future: as soon as I arrive (not 'as soon as I will arrive').
explain.fr: Pour une décision ou une promesse faite en parlant, on utilise will, souvent contracté : I'll. Après « as soon as » et « when », on met le présent, même pour le futur : as soon as I arrive (et non « as soon as I will arrive »). En français on dit « dès que j'arriverai », mais pas en anglais.

examples: I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

feedback.en: Use the present continuous (am + -ing) for something happening now.
feedback.fr: Le présent continu (am + -ing) décrit ce qui se passe maintenant.

practice.prompt: I ____ you as soon as I arrive.

feedback.en: A promise made now uses will: I'll call you.
feedback.fr: Une promesse faite maintenant utilise will : I'll call you.

practice.prompt: I'll call you as soon as I ____ .

feedback.en: After 'as soon as', English uses the present for the future.
feedback.fr: Après « as soon as », l'anglais utilise le présent pour parler du futur.

practice.prompt: There's a lot of ____ on Mombasa Road.

feedback.en: Traffic has no plural and no 'a'.
feedback.fr: « Traffic » n'a pas de pluriel et ne prend pas « a ».

feedback.en: 'By 10:30' means at 10:30 or earlier.
feedback.fr: « By 10:30 » veut dire à 10 h 30 ou avant.

feedback.en: Put the time before 'late': 20 minutes late.
feedback.fr: On place la durée avant « late » : 20 minutes late (≠ « en retard de 20 minutes »).

speak: I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

useIt.prompt: Write a message to Grace: you are 20 minutes late. Say why and give a new time.

lessons.title: Introducing yourself at work

dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Amina. I work in finance.
dialogue.fr: Bonjour, je suis Amina. Je travaille à la comptabilité.

dialogue.text: Nice to meet you, Amina. I'm new. I work with the customer team.
dialogue.fr: Enchantée, Amina. Je suis nouvelle. Je travaille avec l'équipe clients.

dialogue.text: Welcome! What are you working on this week?
dialogue.fr: Bienvenue ! Sur quoi travailles-tu cette semaine ?

dialogue.text: I'm learning our system, and I'm preparing a report for Friday.
dialogue.fr: J'apprends notre système, et je prépare un rapport pour vendredi.

dialogue.text: If you need anything, just ask.
dialogue.fr: Si tu as besoin de quelque chose, n'hésite pas.

words.meaning: a polite greeting the first time you meet someone
words.example: Nice to meet you, Amina.

words.meaning: a group of people who work together
words.example: I work with the customer team.

words.meaning: spend time doing a task
words.example: What are you working on this week?

words.meaning: get something ready
words.example: I'm preparing a report for Friday.

words.meaning: you can ask me any time
words.example: If you need anything, just ask.

pattern.name: present simple vs present continuous

explain.en: Present simple for things that are usually true: I work with the customer team. Present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) for things happening now or around now: I'm preparing a report this week. French uses one present tense for both; English uses two.
explain.fr: Présent simple pour ce qui est habituel ou toujours vrai : I work with the customer team. Présent continu (am/is/are + -ing) pour ce qui se passe maintenant ou en ce moment : I'm preparing a report this week. Le français a un seul présent ; l'anglais en a deux.

examples: I work with the customer team.
This week I'm preparing a report.

practice.prompt: I usually ____ with the customer team.

feedback.en: 'Usually' shows a routine: use the present simple.
feedback.fr: « Usually » indique une habitude : présent simple.

feedback.en: 'This week' is a temporary situation happening now: present continuous.
feedback.fr: « This week » : situation temporaire en cours, donc présent continu.

feedback.en: With he, she or it, the present simple adds -s: she works.
feedback.fr: Avec he, she, it, le présent simple prend -s : she works.

feedback.en: Question form of the present continuous: are + you + -ing.
feedback.fr: Question au présent continu : are + you + -ing.

feedback.en: Present simple questions with 'you' use do.
feedback.fr: Les questions au présent simple avec « you » utilisent do.

feedback.en: The fixed greeting is 'Nice to meet you'.
feedback.fr: La formule fixe est « Nice to meet you ».

speak: Nice to meet you. I work with the customer team.
This week I'm preparing a report.

useIt.prompt: Introduce yourself to a new colleague: your name, what you usually do, and what you are doing this week.

lessons.title: Asking for help in an office

dialogue.text: Excuse me, could you help me with this form?
dialogue.fr: Excusez-moi, pourriez-vous m'aider avec ce formulaire ?

dialogue.text: Of course. Which part is the problem?
dialogue.fr: Bien sûr. Quelle partie pose problème ?

dialogue.text: I'm not sure what to write here. Do I need my ID number?
dialogue.fr: Je ne sais pas quoi écrire ici. Faut-il mon numéro de carte d'identité ?

dialogue.text: Yes, and your phone number below it.
dialogue.fr: Oui, et votre numéro de téléphone en dessous.

dialogue.text: Thank you. Could I bring the copy tomorrow?
dialogue.fr: Merci. Est-ce que je pourrais apporter la copie demain ?

dialogue.text: That's fine. We're open from eight.
dialogue.fr: Pas de problème. Nous ouvrons à huit heures.

words.meaning: a polite way to start talking to someone
words.example: Excuse me, could you help me?

words.meaning: a polite request
words.example: Could you help me with this form?

words.meaning: a paper or page you fill in
words.example: Please fill in this form.

words.meaning: I don't know exactly
words.example: I'm not sure what to write here.

words.meaning: a second paper that is the same as the first
words.example: Could I bring the copy tomorrow?

pattern.name: polite requests

explain.en: Could you + verb asks someone to do something politely: Could you help me? Could I + verb asks for permission: Could I bring it tomorrow? After could, the verb has no 'to' and no -s.
explain.fr: Could you + verbe demande poliment à quelqu'un de faire quelque chose : Could you help me? Could I + verbe demande la permission : Could I bring it tomorrow? Après could, pas de « to » ni de -s.

examples: Could you help me with this form?
Could I bring the copy tomorrow?

practice.prompt: Could you ____ me with this form?

feedback.en: After could, use the verb with no 'to' and no -s.
feedback.fr: Après could, le verbe s'emploie sans « to » et sans -s.

feedback.en: 'Could I…?' asks for permission politely.
feedback.fr: « Could I… ? » demande poliment la permission.

practice.prompt: I'm not sure ____ to write here.

feedback.en: 'I'm not sure what to + verb' is the natural phrase.
feedback.fr: La tournure naturelle est « I'm not sure what to + verbe ».

practice.prompt: The most polite way to start:
options: Excuse me, could you help me?

feedback.en: Start with 'Excuse me' and use 'could you'.
feedback.fr: Commencez par « Excuse me » et utilisez « could you ».

feedback.en: In a do-question the main verb has no -s.
feedback.fr: Dans une question avec do, le verbe principal ne prend pas de -s.

feedback.en: 'Open from eight' gives the opening time.
feedback.fr: « Open from eight » indique l'heure d'ouverture.

speak: Excuse me, could you help me with this form?
Could I bring the copy tomorrow?

useIt.prompt: Write what you would say at an office counter to ask for help with one part of a form.

lessons.title: Calling to book an appointment

dialogue.text: Good morning, Riverside Clinic. How can I help?
dialogue.fr: Bonjour, clinique Riverside. Comment puis-je vous aider ?

dialogue.text: Good morning. I'd like to book an appointment with the doctor, please.
dialogue.fr: Bonjour. Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous avec le médecin, s'il vous plaît.

dialogue.text: Is Tuesday at 11 a.m. OK for you?
dialogue.fr: Mardi à 11 h, ça vous va ?

dialogue.text: I'm afraid I work on Tuesday mornings. Do you have anything in the afternoon?
dialogue.fr: Malheureusement je travaille le mardi matin. Avez-vous quelque chose l'après-midi ?

dialogue.text: We have 3:30 on Wednesday.
dialogue.fr: Nous avons mercredi à 15 h 30.

dialogue.text: That's perfect. I'll see you on Wednesday at 3:30.
dialogue.fr: C'est parfait. À mercredi, 15 h 30.

words.meaning: arrange a time to see someone
words.example: I'd like to book an appointment.

words.meaning: a polite way to say what you want
words.example: I'd like to book an appointment, please.

words.meaning: a polite way to say no or give bad news
words.example: I'm afraid I work on Tuesday mornings.

words.meaning: use 'on' with days
words.example: We have 3:30 on Wednesday.

words.meaning: it suits me
words.example: That's perfect, thank you.

pattern.name: I'd like to + days and times

explain.en: I'd like to + verb is a polite way to say what you want: I'd like to book an appointment. Use 'on' with days (on Wednesday), 'at' with clock times (at 3:30), and 'in' with parts of the day (in the afternoon).
explain.fr: I'd like to + verbe permet de dire poliment ce qu'on veut : I'd like to book an appointment. On met « on » avec les jours (on Wednesday), « at » avec l'heure (at 3:30) et « in » avec les moments de la journée (in the afternoon).

examples: I'd like to book an appointment, please.
I'll see you on Wednesday at 3:30.

feedback.en: After 'I'd like', use to + verb.
feedback.fr: Après « I'd like », on met to + verbe.

practice.prompt: Do you have anything ____ the afternoon?

feedback.en: Use 'in' with parts of the day: in the afternoon.
feedback.fr: On dit « in the afternoon ».

feedback.en: Use 'on' with days.
feedback.fr: On met « on » devant les jours.

feedback.en: Use 'at' with clock times.
feedback.fr: On met « at » devant une heure précise.

practice.prompt: A polite way to say no:

feedback.en: 'I'm afraid…' softens bad news.
feedback.fr: « I'm afraid… » adoucit une réponse négative.

feedback.en: A regular routine: present simple.
feedback.fr: Une habitude : présent simple.

speak: I'd like to book an appointment, please.
I'm afraid I work on Tuesday mornings.

useIt.prompt: Write what you would say to book an appointment, refuse one time politely and accept another.

lessons.title: Writing a short work email

dialogue.text: Hi, can you confirm the time of Thursday's meeting? Thanks, Miriam
dialogue.fr: Bonjour, peux-tu confirmer l'heure de la réunion de jeudi ? Merci, Miriam

dialogue.text: Hi Miriam, the meeting starts at 2 p.m. on Thursday in Room 4. I'm preparing the notes now, and I'll send them before lunch tomorrow. Best regards,
dialogue.fr: Bonjour Miriam, la réunion commence jeudi à 14 h en salle 4. Je prépare les notes en ce moment et je les enverrai demain avant midi. Cordialement,

words.meaning: say that something is correct or certain
words.example: Can you confirm the time?

words.meaning: begins at (for timetables)
words.example: The meeting starts at 2 p.m.

words.meaning: short written points from a meeting
words.example: I'm preparing the notes now.

words.meaning: earlier than lunchtime
words.example: I'll send them before lunch.

words.meaning: a polite way to end an email
words.example: Best regards, Grace

explain.en: A short work email often uses three forms: present simple for a timetable (the meeting starts at 2), present continuous for what you are doing now (I'm preparing the notes), and will for a promise (I'll send them before lunch).
explain.fr: Un court e-mail professionnel utilise souvent trois formes : le présent simple pour un horaire (the meeting starts at 2), le présent continu pour ce que l'on fait en ce moment (I'm preparing the notes) et will pour une promesse (I'll send them before lunch).

practice.prompt: The meeting ____ at 2 p.m. on Thursday.

feedback.en: A timetable uses the present simple; add -s for 'the meeting'.
feedback.fr: Un horaire se dit au présent simple ; -s avec « the meeting ».

feedback.en: An action in progress now: present continuous.
feedback.fr: Une action en cours : présent continu.

feedback.en: A promise about the future: will (I'll) + verb.
feedback.fr: Une promesse pour le futur : will (I'll) + verbe.

practice.prompt: A good way to end a work email:

feedback.en: 'Best regards' is polite and professional.
feedback.fr: « Best regards » est poli et professionnel.

practice.prompt: Can you ____ the time of the meeting?

feedback.en: After 'can you', use the verb with no 'to'.
feedback.fr: Après « can you », le verbe s'emploie sans « to ».

feedback.en: Use 'in' for a room: in Room 4.
feedback.fr: On dit « in Room 4 ».

speak: I'll send the notes before lunch.

useIt.prompt: Write a short email to confirm a meeting time and promise to send something before Friday.
